extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and compiling newspaper stories about wartime operations, official communiqués, casualty counts, policy changes, and human-interest/morale pieces for a general readership. Emphasizes sourcing, verification, descriptive combat accounts, and presentation of opposing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution / label broadcasts and communiqués
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and label the origin of claims and statements (e.g., 'Japanese communique, broadcast from Tokyo', 'U. S. Navy report', 'Tokyo radio', 'Associated Press').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always name the issuing authority and the medium that carried the claim so readers can judge provenance and potential bias; mark explicitly when an item is a radio broadcast, official communique, or departmental report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification / flag unconfirmed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether claims are confirmed by independent or opposing sources (e.g., 'Here is the Japanese score, not confirmed by any Allied source').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting enemy or third-party claims, state whether they have been independently verified and avoid presenting unconfirmed tallies as fact; use qualifiers like 'claimed', 'announced', or 'not confirmed'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present opposing/contrasting accounts side-by-side
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast enemy communiqués with official U.S. or Allied reports to show differences in claimed losses and outcomes (e.g., Japanese communique vs. U. S. Official Report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay out both sides' versions (dates, figures, narrative) to give readers context and highlight discrepancies; where possible, include both verbatim excerpts and summarized tallies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative casualty/loss tabulation with class breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numerical tallies of sunk/damaged ships and aircraft, broken down by class (battleships, heavy cruisers, light cruisers, destroyers, transports, aircraft).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include totals and class-level counts; note when categories are aggregated or combined and explain any parenthetical notations or special aggregations so readers understand how numbers were compiled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain data/aggregation conventions in box scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate tabulations to clarify how categories were combined (e.g., 'the parentheses under Japanese claims ... indicate that the Japanese totalled heavy and light cruisers in one category').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing a boxed score or table, add footnotes or captions that explain nonstandard groupings, date ranges, and whether the score is dated/undated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official reports as primary factual anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on and cite official departmental communiques and Navy/Army/War Department reports (e.g., 'U. S. Official Report', 'Navy Department communique No. ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat official reports as primary sources for losses and actions but still cross-check and present caveats when discrepancies with other sources exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize propaganda and 'saving face' language
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when an enemy statement appears crafted for domestic morale or propaganda (e.g., 'obviously worded to save ‘face at home as well as among the Axis partners').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analysis indicating likely motives behind phrasing and caution readers about accepting such statements at face value; label emotionally loaded or nationalistic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-scene descriptive combat reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Include vivid, sensory descriptions and action details from correspondents or combatants (dogfights, aerobatics, explosions, pilots' maneuvers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first-hand detail and correspondent bylines to convey immediacy and drama, but balance colorful language with accurate factual reporting (dates, losses, outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter credentials and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the reporter's name and role (e.g., 'By Sergeant E. J. Burman Marine Corps Combat Correspondent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show correspondent rank/affiliation when relevant to establish authority and perspective (combat correspondent, AP, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote prominent officials accurately and in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish verbatim quotes from leaders and commanders (e.g., Admiral Halsey's 'Kill Japs. Kill more Japs.'), including setting and occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record exact wording for forceful or controversial statements and provide surrounding context (who said it, where, and why) so readers can assess intent and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest and morale pieces with concrete detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Report personal anecdotes and home-front observations (Mrs. Roosevelt's trip, British restaurants and rationing, soldiers' reactions) to illustrate broader wartime effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific, relatable details (menus, souvenirs, impressions) to humanize coverage while connecting anecdotes to larger policy or morale themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report policy and administrative changes with dates and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover governmental/regulatory actions (Selective Service registration dates, deferment rules, waivers) with precise dates, eligibility, and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State exact deadlines, who is affected, and the operational procedure (how to apply, who decides) so readers can act or understand implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name officials and give titles when reporting claims or disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify speakers with their office or rank (e.g., 'Attorney General Biddle', 'Maj. Gen. Lewis B. Hershey', 'Vice-Admiral William F. Halsey, Jr.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include full name and title to establish accountability and allow readers to judge the source's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag uncertainties and avoid definitive language on contested events
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cautious language where events or outcomes are disputed or only partially reported (e.g., 'claimed', 'reported', 'was said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting contested enemy claims or unconfirmed details as settled facts; provide qualifiers and, where possible, follow-up commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document ceremonial/award announcements from official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Report formal honors and decorations announced by governments (e.g., Emperor conferred Order of the Golden Kite on X officers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the announcing body (Board of Decorations, War Ministry) and provide numbers, names, and campaign context when available.
